plans.note: Section 7 is captioned 'Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor' and is the controlling location. Check whether the cap is mutual or one-way in Contractor's favour, whether the cap amount is tied to fees paid, and whether carve-outs (IP infringement, confidentiality, gross negligence/wilful misconduct, indemnity obligations) survive the cap.

The heading of sec-7 runs the wrong direction — it provides indemnification OF the Contractor, i.e. an indemnity from us. Expect no Vendor-side third-party IP/misconduct indemnity anywhere; confirm sec-5 (reps/warranties) does not carry one before treating the Vendor indemnity as missing, and separately assess whether our indemnity in sec-7 is unacceptably broad.

No covenants/restrictive-covenant section appears in the outline. Scan sec-1 (Purpose of Engagement) for any limitation on the business we may conduct or competing products we may build or buy; otherwise the rule is inapplicable and no comment is needed.

Exclusivity, if present, would sit in the scope language of sec-1 or as a sole-source condition on compensation in sec-3. Note the outline skips section 2, which may contain scope/term language not shown — verify before concluding absence.

Pricing terms live in sec-3 (Contractor's Compensation). Look for any best-pricing or most-favoured-customer language; only an MFN running against us is a deviation, an MFN in our favour is left alone.

Consultant-style agreements often place a no-hire of Contractor personnel near the engagement or termination provisions. Check sec-1 and sec-6; if present, confirm it is time-limited, mutual and carves out general advertising.

Section 6 (Termination) is the controlling location. Confirm we hold a convenience right on reasonable notice without termination fees, and that the Contractor cannot terminate for convenience mid-engagement; check any wind-down payment obligation in sec-3.

No term/renewal heading appears; term mechanics may sit in the unnumbered gap at section 2 or inside sec-6. Look for evergreen renewal, the non-renewal notice window and any uncapped price uplift on renewal.

The outline shows no miscellaneous/general provisions section, so governing law and venue may be absent or buried in the preamble or a trailing paragraph of sec-7. If genuinely absent, flag as missing rather than deviation.

No assignment heading in the outline; check the closing paragraphs of sec-6 and the preamble's party/successor language. Confirm we may assign to affiliates and successors and that the Contractor gains no termination right on our change of control.

Section 4 (Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance) governs. Verify deliverables vest in us on creation or on payment, that pre-existing Clear Capital materials and our data are not assigned to the Contractor, and that any Contractor background-IP retention is paired with a licence we can actually use.

Any licence-back of Contractor tools or background IP will sit in sec-4 alongside the ownership language. Check that the grant extends to our affiliates and contractors and is not revocable at the Contractor's discretion; cross-check sec-6 for termination-triggered licence revocation.

Audit rights against us, if any, would attach to compensation verification in sec-3 or usage of materials in sec-4. Only audits of Clear Capital are in scope; confirm frequency, notice, location and cost allocation if found.
Look for late-payment penalties, kill fees or stipulated damages payable by us in sec-3, and for any penalty language carved out of the liability cap in sec-7. Credits running to us are not flagged.

Section 5 pairs reps and warranties with a warranty disclaimer, so expect a narrow or disclaimed warranty. Assess the warranty period, conformity to Specifications, and whether the remedy is real (re-performance/refund); read with the acceptance mechanic in sec-4 and avoid double-flagging the disclaimer under LOL-CAP.

No insurance heading appears in the outline. Check sec-5 and the risk-allocation language in sec-7; if the Contractor's personnel touch our data or premises and there is no coverage obligation, treat as missing.
Any minimum hours, retainer floor or take-or-pay commitment would appear in sec-3, with scope framing in sec-1. If a minimum exists, confirm it is escapable via the termination right in sec-6.

Post-termination consequences would sit at the end of sec-6, with return of materials possibly handled by the ownership language in sec-4. Confirm whether we get return of our data and reasonable transition assistance; if neither, flag as missing.
